epics.title: Internal Operations and Admin Dashboard
epics.jtbd: When managing the site's internal operations, I want an admin dashboard, so that I can efficiently track, assign, and complete work items. Goal: Streamline internal site operations. Q1: How many tasks are currently open? Q2: What is the average time to complete a task? Metric: Average operational task completion time.
requirements: R1: The admin team can capture a new operational work item and assign it to a team member.
R2: The admin team can track the current state of a work item on the dashboard.
R3: The admin team can complete a work item and view summary reports on completed items.
R4: The UI must be fully responsive and usable on a mobile phone.
R5: Every action gets visible feedback (success, failure, or progress), and user input survives failed submissions.
R6: Destructive actions are explicitly confirmed before they happen.
R7: The UI must be fully accessible (WCAG 2.1 level AA) including keyboard operability, labelled form controls, and visible focus.
R8: The dashboard backend must securely persist data and authorize requests.
R9: The system must implement GQM to measure operational efficiency (Goal: Streamline operations; Qs: Open tasks? Time to complete?; Metric: Average task completion time).

slices.title: Admin Dashboard Database Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing data storage for this epic, I want to define the relational schema, so that the admin dashboard has reliable work item persistence.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a need to store operational work items,
When the database schema is applied,
Then tables for work items, assignments, and states are created via Flyway migrations.
Given the new tables,
When querying for dashboard reports,
Then appropriate indexes are present to support efficient state tracking.

slices.title: Admin Dashboard API Backend
slices.jtbd: When implementing backend services for this epic, I want to expose secure endpoints, so that the frontend can manage operational tasks.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an authorized admin client,
When creating or updating a work item,
Then the backend validates the payload and correctly persists the state.
Given an unauthorized request,
When accessing the dashboard endpoints,
Then a 403 Forbidden or 401 Unauthorized response is returned.

slices.title: Admin Dashboard API Contract Definition
slices.jtbd: When preparing for parallel development for this epic, I want to define the shared API contract, so that frontend and backend teams have a stable integration point.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the dashboard requirements,
When the API contract is authored,
Then all necessary REST endpoints and DTOs are documented.
Given the defined contract,
When reviewed by the engineering teams,
Then both frontend and backend developers approve the schema.

slices.title: Admin Dashboard Frontend Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the UI for this epic, I want to build responsive and accessible components, so that admins can easily manage operations.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the dashboard UI on a mobile device,
When the admin views work items,
Then the layout adapts successfully without horizontal scrolling.
Given an admin action like creating a task,
When the action completes or fails,
Then visible feedback is displayed and input data is not lost on failure.
Given the WCAG 2.1 level AA requirements,
When the UI is interacted with,
Then all form controls are labeled, focus is visible, and it is fully keyboard operable.
Given a destructive action like deletion,
When the admin initiates it,
Then an explicit confirmation dialogue is presented before execution.

slices.title: Admin Dashboard QA Verification
slices.jtbd: When finalizing the epic, I want to verify all features end-to-end, so that the admin dashboard works reliably before release.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the fully integrated system,
When loaded with realistic mock operational work items,
Then the admin can traverse the capture, assign, track, and complete paths end-to-end.
Given the test pyramid policy,
When the test suite executes,
Then unit tests verify logic, integration tests verify API contracts, and E2E tests verify the critical admin journey.
Given the goal to measure efficiency,
When tasks are completed,
Then telemetry data for task completion time is successfully captured and verified.
